From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Mar 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOW schedule + tier pricing question — Pioneer Health

Jordan — I had a quick pass on the redline. High-level guidance below and a couple of suggested text snippets. I put line comments in the attached PDF for reference.

1) Temporary top-up: we can do a credit-based top-up for 60 days, but we must explicitly state that it does not alter the baseline committed capacity in the MSA/order form. Suggested clause: "Temporary Capacity Addendum: The Parties agree that any temporary capacity or credit applied under this addendum is time-limited and will not be construed as an amendment to the baseline committed capacity absent an executed written amendment signed by authorized representatives."

2) Discount window: we should avoid open-ended discount clauses. Propose language: "Discount applies for the specified window of 90 days beginning on the effective date of the addendum; thereafter standard pricing applies unless otherwise mutually agreed in writing."

3) Audit & reconciliation: include clear usage reporting cadence and the right to audit usage records within a 30-day reconciliation period. If Pioneer wants system-level logs, we'll provide redacted summaries.

4) Early start (April 1): If Pioneer requires an earlier start, we need a grace period clause for implementation (upto 14 days) or a phased activation schedule to protect operational SLAs.

5) Implementation SOW exhibit: instead of changing the MSA, recommend adding an Exhibit C (Implementation & Ramp) that captures the April start, the 60-day top-up mechanics, and acceptance criteria. That keeps the MSA stable and makes the change surgical.

I attached legal_comments_pioneer_redline.pdf with line-level notes and a proposed one-paragraph addendum draft you can share. If procurement prefers option B (short-term committed bump), we'll need a minimal minimum-guarantee and a termination notice period (90 days) called out.

Let me know if you want me on the call tomorrow.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Asha / team — summary and next steps.

Summary of our position (two options):
A) Temporary top-up (recommended short-term): Redwood applies a credit-based top-up for 60 days, with explicit language that this does not change the baseline commitment. Discount applies for 90 days from the addendum effective date. Billing reconciliation occurs within 30 days after the top-up period.
B) Short-term committed bump: Pioneer signs a 90-day committed bump with a minimum-guarantee and a 90-day notice to unwind; this requires a minimal amendment to the order form and a short note in the MSA about the temporary fee schedule.

Laura has drafted model language and recommended using an Exhibit C (Implementation & Ramp) for the April start so we avoid touching the MSA. Attached is a one-page options summary and a clean redline for your internal review.

Please confirm: 1) which option you prefer (A or B), and 2) who from procurement should be on the joint call. I propose Wed 03/12 10:00–10:30 PT. If you need a different time, say so.

Attaching: capacity_options_20250311.pdf (summary of A/B options + rough financials).

Thanks,
Jordan
